open_questions: Centroid is inconclusive (why: no sector with a clear difference image) so on-target not independently confirmed by difference imaging, though neighbour check favors it.
Only refit.transits=3 with gaps.p_chance 0.007383; more transits would further rule out a few-event false alarm.
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a steady 694 ppm, 3.5-hour flat-bottomed dip repeating every 12.9 days that matches the 0.8 solar-radius star's duration and predicts a 2.3 Earth-radius planet. Sector-to-sector and transit-to-transit depths are consistent and no nearby star can plausibly be the source at this precision, with no odd/even or secondary eclipses detected. The 3-transit detection with moderate signal-to-noise is best explained by a small planet on a nearby star.

reasons.why: 2.3 R_Earth is in the planet regime, well below 10 R_Earth planet/giant boundary, with rp_over_rstar 0.02648.
Negative v_sigma favors flat-bottomed rather than V-shaped eclipse; best_ingress_fraction 0.2 and fit chi2_red 0.9996 with fit_b 0.3927 consistent with central transit.

Observed duration 3.498 h vs central 3.625 h (ratio 0.9651) matches TIC radius 0.7969 Rsun / Gaia ratio 0.9967; fit_log_density_ratio -0.03985 and star_density_penalty -0.00003314 show no duration mismatch.

Depth steady between sectors (731 ppm sector 3 err 126, 658 ppm sector 30 err 78) with p_constant 0.6184 and transit_depths p_consistent 0.8145 across 3 transits, share 1.0 of signal; no evidence for a few bad events.
No star within 21 arcsec can produce the dip at <=25% eclipse, closest that could is 75 arcsec needing 0.0135 eclipse, ruling out a close blended eclipsing binary despite contratio 0.0009109.

Secondary at phase 0.6354 has SNR 3.78 below 5 threshold and is not significant vs best_brightening_snr 3.452 (ratio 1.095); no odd_even difference available and no phase_curve excess (amplitude 100.9 ppm ratio_to_depth 0.144) to indicate a stellar companion.
